name: U.S. Physical Therapy Inc
business: Operates outpatient physical therapy clinics for orthopedic, sports and work injuries, plus onsite injury prevention services for Fortune 500 employers and insurers.

events.what: No CEO change. Premise of a 2024 to 2025 Reading to Williams CEO handoff is not supported: Chris Reading has been CEO since 2004 and added Chairman on 2024-05-21; Eric Williams was promoted to President (continuing as COO East) on 2024-05-21, outside the window. Reading still CEO and Chairman on the Q2 2026 call and in the 2026 DEF 14A.
events.who: Christopher J. Reading (CEO), Eric Williams (President and COO East)

events.what: CFO Carey Hendrickson resigned to take another public-company CFO role; Jason Curtis (SVP Finance and Accounting) interim CFO

events.from: Omnicell (former EVP and CFO); earlier Essilor of America, J&J Vision
Texas Children's Hospital (EVP and Chief Information Innovation Officer)

events.what: Hospital affiliation agreements (NYU Langone via Metro partnership, plus a Gulf Coast system) phasing in during H2 2026; tuck-in acquisitions in 2026 totaling $38 million purchase price (no Item 2.01 8-K)
events.who: NYU Langone; Gulf Coast hospital partner
events.source: document_id 140879; document_id 140878 (first Metro clinics began phasing in the week before the 2026-05-07 call); document_id 130428

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework event found in Baba corpus or 8-Ks. Next touchpoint is the Q3 2026 earnings call (early November 2026, date not in corpus), the new CFO's first call; 2027 guidance would normally come with the Q4 call (FY2026 guide was given 2026-02-26, document_id 140879).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: No margin level or annual bps target. The only dated numeric figure is a dollar EBITDA contribution: at least $7.3 million of USPH adjusted EBITDA (at least $14 million at the partnership level) from the two hospital affiliations in 2027. That is a growth contribution, not a cost saving or a margin target. FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide $102 million to $106 million. Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years (December FYE).

statements.quote: As discussed in our release, those original clinics will provide an enterprise lift for these two partnerships of at least $14 million in EBITDA in 2027, and a USPH portion after minority interest of over $7 million.
statements.speaker: Chris Reading
statements.doc_title: U.S. Physical Therapy Inc Q4 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: When fully implemented, which we expect to happen by year-end 2026, these two hospital affiliation agreements are expected to contribute at least $14 million on a combined basis to our PT revenue and income, with a corresponding impact to USPH's adjusted EBITDA of at least $7.3 million, reflecting our ownership interest
statements.speaker: Carey Hendrickson
statements.doc_title: U.S. Physical Therapy Inc Q4 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: Taking into account the year-to-date 2026 results and the expected increasing benefit of hospital affiliations in the back half of the year, we are reaffirming our full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $102 million-$106 million.
statements.speaker: Jason Curtis
statements.doc_title: U.S. Physical Therapy Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: No margin level stated, so no bps gap. The $7.3 million 2027 hospital contribution is 7.0% of FY2026 consensus EBITDA ($104.0 million); FY2027 consensus EBITDA ($118.0 million) is already $14.0 million above FY2026, so the street very likely already carries it. D scored on the no-level rule (4-month revision +2.9%).
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), data_comps revisions asof 2026-10-01

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026]. Q1 from VA actuals; Q2 2026 from interim CFO on the call (revenue $214 million, adjusted EBITDA $27.0 million, document_id 130428; not yet in VA actuals). Margin compressed on self-insured medical claims (about $3.2 million swing) and front-loaded hiring for hospital clinics; PT adjusted gross margin 19.9% vs 21.4%. LTM 11.8% is Q3 2025 to Q2 2026.

verdict: Score flatters the setup: a 22-year CEO, a new external CFO one month in, and a dated $7.3 million hospital EBITDA contribution the street likely already models; weak GXO match.
open_questions: Does new CFO Nchacha Etta (ex Omnicell) bring a margin or cost framework at the Q3 2026 call or with 2027 guidance?
Is the $7.3 million 2027 hospital EBITDA contribution already inside the $118.0 million FY2027 consensus, and how much more do additional hospital deals add?
Is the Q1 and Q2 2026 margin compression (medical claims, pre-hiring) transitory, and does WelcomeWare front-desk virtualization show up as a quantified saving?
